diagnostics.message: :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

The explicit depends_on on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant: the module already depends on the log group implicitly through the `logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda.name` attribute reference.

The explicit depends_on on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant: the event target already depends on the module implicitly via `arn = module.forge_trust_validator_lambda.lambda_function_arn`.

null_resource.update_forge_role_trust embeds the ARN of the IAM role created by module.forge_trust_validator_lambda ("arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator") into the forge roles' assume-role policy via a local-exec provisioner. Since the ARN is interpolated from var.prefix rather than referencing the module, Terraform orders them independently; if the provisioner runs before the validator role exists, `aws iam update-assume-role-policy` fails with an invalid-principal error. Add a dependency so the lambda module (and its IAM role) is created first.
